Abstract: Background: Tricuspid valve surgery is indicated for severe symptomatic tricuspid valve regurgitation (TR) when performed concomitant to another cardiac operation. While percutaneous therapies for TR continue to advance, anatomic constraints may necessitate consideration of surgery in some patients. Methods: Herein, we provide a contemporary review of surgical techniques used to treat TR, which can serve as a complement to existing and emerging tricuspid valve treatment therapies. Results: We performed a literature review on established surgical tricuspid repair techniques. Conclusions: Surgical repair of the tricuspid valve is safe and feasible. While annuloplasty remains the cornerstone operative strategy, leaflet and sub-valvular techniques serve as adjuncts to help successful repair. The therapeutic paradigm for TR continues to evolve.
